### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, five activities — A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 — each ran in roughly 16–24 of 100 traces and were mutually exclusive alternatives (pairs of them almost never co-occurred), with A43, which appears in every trace, followed by one of them in about 99 of 100 of its observed outgoing transitions. In the later window they have nearly vanished: A26 and A27 were not observed at all, A19 and A25 each appear in 1 of 200 traces, and A20 in 3 of 200. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, DIR007, REL010, REL014, REL016, REL019, REL022]

- Before, these five activities bridged A43 to A28: A20, A25, A26 and A27 led almost exclusively to A28 (about 97–100 of 100 of their outgoing transitions), A20 ran after A43 in about 24 of 100 traces and before A28 in about 24 of 100, and A25 and A27 showed the same pattern (about 20–21 of 100). In the later window, about 92 of 100 of A43's outgoing transitions go directly to A28, and all of these co-occurrences and orderings with the five activities have collapsed to about 0–1.5 of 100. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL017, REL018, REL021, REL023, REL024]

- The path shortened by about one step: A28 now immediately follows A43 in about 93 of 100 cases (before, it followed two positions later in about 99 of 100), the distance from A16 to A28 fell from five positions (about 99 of 100) to four (about 89 of 100), and A15 followed by A28 within five steps — seen in 1 of 200 traces before — occurs in 100 of 200 traces after. [LAG011, LAG008, LAG004]

- A02 also changed: it ran in 27 of 100 traces before versus 14 of 100 after, its mean position moved from about 0.31 to about 0.49 of the trace length, and its outgoing transitions shifted from about 77 of 100 leading to A16 to a spread over A49 (about 21), A16 (about 18), A28 (about 18) and A15 (about 14). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001]

- Smaller shifts: A15 and A16 now occur slightly later in the trace and A28 slightly earlier; A15's outgoing transitions to A02 fell from about 13 to about 1 in 100. [POS002, POS003, POS009, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the segment of five mutually exclusive activities A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 that previously connected A43 to A28 is bypassed: A43 now leads directly to A28, and the five activities are executed in at most about 1–3 of 200 traces (A26 and A27 not at all), whereas before each of them ran in about 16–24 of 100 traces as the link between A43 and A28. [DIR007, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, LAG011]

Screening expected well under one qualifying item (about 0.72) if nothing had changed, yet 57 items qualified, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. The behavioural signs are also direct and consistent: A43's successor profile flipped from the five activities to A28, the A43→A28 and A16→A28 distances each shortened by one position, and the five activities' participation, their co-occurrence with A43 and A28, and the orderings A43→A20/A25/A27 and A20/A27→A28 all disappeared together. [DIR007, LAG011, LAG008, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL017, REL018, REL021, REL023, REL024]

Limitations: with 0–3 observations of the five activities in the later window, the evidence shows they are no longer executed in practice but cannot distinguish whether they were removed from the process or remain as a path that is simply never chosen — zero participation only means the activity was not observed. The apparent new successors of A20 and A25 rest on 3 and 1 observations and are weak. [DIR003, DIR004, OCC005, OCC006]

Other differences: A02's participation halved (27 to 14 of 100 traces), it now occurs later in the trace, and its successors shifted from mostly A16 to a spread including A49, A28 and A15, while A15's transitions into A02 largely disappeared; this could be an independent change or a side effect of the bypass, which the evidence cannot decide. A15, A16 and A28 show only minor positional shifts. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR002, POS002, POS003, POS009]
